title: Dancing at Quiroste
description: 2008 mural by Ann Thiermann for the UC Santa Cruz American Indian Resource Center.  This painting depicts a Quiroste Nation village site in Quiroste Valley (within contemporary Año Nuevo State Park). Many designs in this painting were based off of the 1769 Portola Expedition, which encountered the Quiroste, as well as the oral histories from the Amah Mutsun Nation. The Quiroste, among the larger nations near Big Basin, shared common language, practices, and beliefs with other neighboring nations of the Santa Cruz Mountains (known as Mak-sah-re-jah, meaning "Sharp Ridged Mountain of the Eagle"). This mural illustrates some of those common beliefs with the inclusion of the hummingbird on the lefthand side and the coyote silhouette in the clouds, two animals common to Mutsun creation stories.
creator: Ann Thiermann
location: UC Santa Cruz American Indian Resource Center
credit: Ann Thiermann, 2008

title: California Redwood Park, 1915
description:
Collector Leonard McKay writes, "This painting was displayed in the second year of the Panama Pacific Exposition in San Francisco, celebrating the opening of the Panama Canal and the rebuilding of San Francisco after the 1906 Earthquake and fire. This is one of Andrew Hill's finest paintings. California Redwood Park was later renamed Big Basin Redwoods State Park. Hill led the fight to save the redwoods and was one of the most important early conservationists. 

Standing at the base of the redwood tree are the female members of the McPherson family and seated to the right is Carrie Stephens Walter, who worked alongside Hill in the successful effort to acquire Big Basin. The McPherson family owned the Santa Cruz Sentinal and were influentual in the drive to save the redwoods. For more information on Hill, read Carolyn de Vries excellent book 'Grand and Ancient Forest.'"
creator: Andrew P. Hill
credit: Leonard McKay Collection; Collection of History San Jose

title: Scene from The Soul of Sequoia
description: The Sempervirens Club sponsored and managed a stageplay to be performed outdoors titled "The Soul of Sequoia." Bridging Indigineous imagery with club rhetoric, many supporters of the play believed it to be a climax for the club. The play followed the story of Indigenous peoples and a character titled the "Spirit of Man" confronting woodsmen that threatened the sacred redwood trees within the grove. The play seemed to have only been performed a limited number of times due to funding constraints, but its playbook can be found online on HathiTrust.
creator: Andrew P. Hill
credit: Big Basin Park Photograph Album; Collection of History San Jose

title: Hotel at Boulder Creek
description: The Sempervirens Club often rendezvoused here at Henry L. Middleton's Commercial Hotel, where he helped provide lodging and camping equipment for their continuous expeditions into Big Basin. Even as a large stockholder to a lumber company, Middleton became greatly interested in Big Basin's preservation and continued to support the club for almost two decades. The caption reads, "13 miles by wagon road to Big Basin."
creator: Andrew P. Hill
credit: Sempervirens Club Records; Collection of History San Jose
